Message:
fix(freshness-monitor): hermetically stub notify_via_flow_doctor by default (#743)

test_handler_per_spec_exception_does_not_sink_pass enabled
FRESHNESS_MONITOR_ENABLED=true but never re-stubbed notify_via_flow_doctor
after its importlib.reload(index), so the per-spec-exception (probe_failed)
path called the REAL Telegram notifier whenever this suite ran with live
AWS/Telegram credentials ambient — paging the live ops-health channel with
fixture data on 2026-07-11 (alpha-engine-config#2208).

Replace flow_doctor_telegram in sys.modules with a safe no-op BEFORE any
test's import/reload of index, mirroring scheduled-groom-dispatcher's
_install_stubs fleet pattern, so a test can no longer reach the real
notifier just by forgetting a monkeypatch. Apply the same hardening to
groom-liveness-probe and usage-pace-alert, whose per-test wiring was
currently safe but fragile against the same class of gap. Also add a
deterministic backstop in notify_via_flow_doctor itself: refuse to
dispatch when context["owner_repo"] is a known test-fixture namespace
(ae-test, alpha-engine-test), independent of any test-suite stubbing.

Author: Brian McMahon
Message:
fix(daily_closes): scrub FRED api_key from error logs + retry FRED 5xx (#220)

requests.exceptions.HTTPError.str() embeds the full request URL —
including ``api_key=<credential>`` — in its message. The existing
``_fetch_fred_closes`` except-block logged that raw via
``logger.warning("FRED fetch failed for %s (%s): %s", t, sid, e)`` so
any FRED 5xx in production MorningEnrich / EOD dumped the credential
to CloudWatch.

Surfaced 2026-05-12 during the post-merge repair run for PR #219 — a
transient FRED 500 on VXVCLS during the operator step leaked the key
to the conversation transcript. The FRED key is rotated separately;
this commit closes the leak class.

Changes:
- ``_scrub_api_key(msg) -> str`` helper in ``collectors/daily_closes.py``
  masks the ``api_key=...`` querystring fragment with ``api_key=***``
- ``_fetch_fred_closes`` warn-log routes the exception through the
  scrubber
- Repair script's ``_fetch_fred_range`` already added retry+scrub in
  the cherry-pick from the live-debug session; this commit consolidates
  by importing the shared ``_scrub_api_key`` from ``daily_closes`` so
  the regex doesn't drift across files

Tests (+7, suite 792 → 799):
- ``_scrub_api_key`` masks URL-embedded keys, handles exception objects
  directly, passthroughs when no key present, terminates at ``&``
- ``_fetch_fred_closes`` warn-log scrub regression
- ``_fetch_fred_range`` retry-warn + final-error scrub regressions

Description: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations.
Author: Brian McMahon
Message:
fix(groom-dispatcher): truncate run_token in alert bodies — it wedges the alert-drain (#1216)

A bare `run_token=<32 lowercase hex>` in a lane-death / lane-reclaimed
notification body matches gitleaks' stock `generic-api-key` rule: the keyword
`token` adjacent to a high-entropy 32-char value is exactly that rule's shape.
It is not a credential — it is a correlation id this Lambda mints per lane.

Where it hurts is downstream. `_notify_cycle` publishes onto the Overseer intake
bus; alert-drain reads the queue into its LLM request; the DLP egress proxy
gitleaks-scans that outbound body and returns HTTP 400. The drain agent exits
rc=1, and because nothing is deleted from the queue without a ledger record
(overseer-policy.md invariant 8) the same message is re-read by the next run.

One lane-death alert therefore wedges the entire response plane indefinitely —
and the SQS retry ladder (`maxReceiveCount: 5`) drags the queue's *other*
messages into the DLQ five receives at a time while it does.

Measured 2026-08-03, reproduced locally against the fleet's own
`gitleaks-egress.toml` at gitleaks 8.30.1:

  - 12 of 79 sampled intake messages matched `generic-api-key`
  - every one of them from `flow-doctor:scheduled-groom-dispatcher`
  - every one of them on the `run_token=` field, in `detail.body`
  - four consecutive drain runs dead (alpha-engine-config-I6191, occurrence 4)
  - truncating the body token clears the match; scanning the post-fix message
    yields zero findings

12 hex chars stays long enough to correlate a body against the dispatch ledger
by eye. The FULL token is unchanged everywhere it is machine-read — `dedup_key`,
the `context` payload, and every log line — so truncation is a rendering change
and nothing programmatic is affected.

Guard observed failing (overseer-policy.md invariant 13): restoring the full
token to the body turns `test_lane_death_body_truncates_the_run_token` red.

Does NOT clear the messages already queued — those are immutable. See
alpha-engine-config-I6294 for the structural half.

Author: claude[bot]
Message:
shadow-morning: grade the ArcticDB row, then dispatch the gate (#1924)

The shadow-morning workload never ran `python -m shadow arctic-parity`, so
every same-day parity report kept `arcticdb/universe` as `in_region_only`,
which the gate counts as an exception (alpha-engine-config-I11546).

- shadow-morning now runs arctic-parity for $TD after parity (on parity's
  exit 0 or 1, never on 2), and --dispatch-gate moves from parity onto it.
  Exit order: failed leg, then parity's 2, then arctic-parity's code.
- arctic-parity gains --await-live-unit/--await-timeout-seconds: it waits
  for v1's D18 manifest for the day to read ok before comparing. v1's
  morning-arctic-append measured 12:22-12:55Z on 09-22..24, after the
  ~12:30Z publish, and ArcticDB has no manifest-pinned version to grade
  against. A timeout exits 2 with the report untouched.
- arctic-parity --dispatch-gate dispatches after a refused or failed
  comparison too, whenever a published report exists.
- rewrite_report keeps the summary counts the report declared
  (settling_bar_keys, live_superseded, not_applicable) instead of
  rebuilding from a fixed list.
- shadow-morning runtime cap 3600 -> 7200: legs plus parity measured
  42-45 min, plus up to 45 min of waiting and ~2 min of comparison.

Message:
fix(spot): demote a reclaimed pool and escalate the final attempt to on-demand (alpha-engine-config-I11565) (#1944)

rehearsal-2026-09-24-1 failed at DataPhase1 after four consecutive c6i.large
reclaims: the launcher's own relaunch and the SF's DataPhase1Reissue each
walked INSTANCE_TYPES from its head (c6i.large since I11412), and nothing
ever fell back to on-demand.

New infrastructure/_spot_relaunch.sh, sourced by _spot_common.sh and the
spot_data_weekly.sh monolith (same one-file shape as _stage_window.sh):

- Every confirmed reclaim (relaunch-decision classification=reclaim, hold
  verdicts included) records the box's type and subnet in a per-run file on
  the launcher host, keyed by RUN_TOKEN (the SF execution name that
  ssm_log_capture exports), so the SF reissue on the same box inherits it.
  Later launches in the run move those to the back of the rotation.
- The final attempt of a relaunch chain launches on-demand via
  `krepis.ec2_spot launch --no-spot`, the same primitive
  launch_with_fallback's on-demand rung calls, tagged LaunchMarket /
  LaunchReason (force_on_demand after a reclaim, capacity_exhausted after
  an all-pools refusal). Every launch now carries those provenance tags.

Whether to relaunch, and how often, stays with krepis relaunch-decision.

Message:
feat(parity): recompute-lineage v1_cause evidence for D31 feature keys (alpha-engine-config-I11203) (#1952)

* fix(parity): settling forgives only numeric moves; JSON series declare a row_date settling bar (alpha-engine-config-I11551)

1. Inside a key_date- or row_date-settling key, only a numeric value move
   (price, volume, derived numeric) is recorded as settling. Identity fields
   (bar_date, currency, labels, dates) and membership stay strict on the
   trading day too. eod_closes/{date}.json had graded `match` on 09-21..23
   while the shadow's EU rows carried bar_date D-1 (hid I11548).
   same_day_snapshot is unchanged.

2. x-settling-bar.row_dates lets a JSON key declare where its row dates are
   (`$.series.*[*][0]`). metron_close_history declares it for
   close_history/consolidated.json only. A row settles only when both sides
   date it trading_day; a length diff, a differing date and every earlier
   row stay strict. The next report grades the day-D rows strictly in a
   `prior_day` block, the same way price_cache already is. The loader
   refuses a malformed declaration. resolve_contract now prefers the most
   specific template, so consolidated.json is no longer shadowed by
   {sym}.json.

No band widened, no key excluded.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01PU9ghbMcx3RDSd8V2om4v1
Signed-off-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(parity): `v1_cause` verdict for differences proven v1-side, with inline evidence (alpha-engine-config-I11203)

Implements Brian's 2026-09-24 ruling ("proven v1 cause") on #11203.

A mismatch row is re-graded `v1_cause` only when every breach is explained
by machine-checked evidence, which is recorded on the row:

1. v1_bar_provisional: v1's own manifest stamps the key
   `bar_settlement: provisional` and the shadow's stamps it `settled`.
   Applies only to numeric breaches of a key_date key.
2. vendor_published_after_v1_fetch: the shadow's extra trailing
   observations were each first released on a later day than the
   vendor's last_updated for the version v1 read. The shared prefix must
   agree.

Schema, membership, coverage, frame row count and identity fields are
never explained. Partial evidence is published as `v1_cause_refused`.

- Report: schema v3, `summary.v1_cause`, `prior_day_settled.v1_cause`,
  and `values.identity_breaches` on frame rows. `met` passes
  match or v1_cause.
- Gate: read_parity counts v1_cause as explained and prints it apart
  from match, for both rows and D-1 pairs.
- Evidence is read from the manifest attempt that recorded the key, not
  the latest attempt.
- Producers: D20 stamps bar_settlement on its closes keys. D23 records
  FRED last_updated and first-release dates as manifest guards.

No band widened, no key excluded.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01PU9ghbMcx3RDSd8V2om4v1
Signed-off-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(parity): D17 stamps bar_settlement; xsource_provenance is provenance (alpha-engine-config-I11559)

Two v1_cause evidence gaps from the replay of 09-22 and 09-23:

1. D17 now stamps `bar_settlement` on staging/daily_closes. The D-1 re-check
   grades the object D17's morning run left behind, so v1_cause kind 1 reads
   D17's manifest. D17 already computed the stamp, because
   daily_closes.collect(source="polygon_only") returns the same
   dates.bar_settlement_guard_entry reading D19 records. D17 is a whole-mode
   unit, though. Its collector result sits in result["collectors"] and was
   never folded. `_run_whole_mode_unit` now folds the nested collectors
   `_MODE_GUARD_COLLECTORS` names for the mode (morning_enrich ->
   daily_closes), before the status checks, so a failure manifest carries
   them too. The rule is the same as D19/D20. D17 fetches the morning after
   the session, so its verdict is `settled`, and a D-1 difference on this key
   stays strict.

2. staging_daily_closes declares `xsource_provenance` as `x-provenance: true`.
   The observer's audit string embeds the vendor and price. The price is still
   graded strictly in `Close`, and the vendor in `source`.

features/{D-1}/* (D31) is unchanged and stays strict. No column-level lineage
is built.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01PU9ghbMcx3RDSd8V2om4v1

* fix(D17): grade carried-over rows on the object they came from (alpha-engine-config-I11559)

The 09-23 replay showed that D17's fetch-time stamp alone is false for part
of the file. Polygon does not serve CPRI or SAM, so D17's 2026-09-22 file
carried v1 D19's 16:06 ET yfinance cells for them (provisional). Those were
the only rows that differed from the shadow's. A single `settled` reading
would have claimed the whole key was settled.

`daily_closes._settlement_guards` now records a second `bar_settlement`
reading when the polygon_only coalesce carries rows over from the existing
object (retained or downgrade-blocked). That reading is graded on the
object's write time, the rule D19's post-close skip path already uses. When
the two readings disagree, `shadow.parity._bar_settlement_stamp` reads the
key as ambiguous, and the row stays strict.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01PU9ghbMcx3RDSd8V2om4v1
Signed-off-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(parity): row-level v1_cause evidence for carried provisional rows (alpha-engine-config-I11563)

D17 (and D19) now stamp each row they carry over from the existing object
with its own bar_settlement reading, keyed `<key>#<ticker>` and graded on
that object's write time. The run's fetch reading stays the reading for every
row it fetched.

Parity reads the stamps row by row. A key_date frame whose whole-key stamp is
ambiguous is re-graded v1_cause only when every row holding a numeric breach
reads provisional on v1's side and settled on the shadow's. A carried
`settled` reading is never taken on trust: it is followed back through the
earlier writes of the key to the run that fetched the row. Every other breach
stays strict; no band is widened and no key excluded.

_grade_v1_cause now records v1_cause_refused on every mismatch row it grades,
including a row with no evidence at all.

* feat(parity): recompute-lineage v1_cause evidence for D31 feature keys (alpha-engine-config-I11203)

features/{D}/*.parquet is derived and stamps no settlement of its own, so no
existing evidence kind can explain it and it reads unsettled on every report.
This adds a third kind, recompute_lineage, as a counterfactual proof:

- D31 records what it read (features/input_record.py): each S3 object at
  its VersionId, large per-ticker directories as one digested set, each
  ArcticDB library read as a content digest plus the as_of moment, and the
  split-restatement outcome. weekly_collector folds them into the D31 run
  manifest. Effective from the next v1 run; earlier manifests carry none.
- D31 no longer reads day-D rows from ArcticDB (the daily_closes delta is
  the only source of day D). This is a no-op on v1's schedule and closes the
  leak where the shadow's D31 read v1's D32-appended bar.
- shadow/recompute_lineage.py re-runs D31's own build over each side's
  recorded inputs: read-only pinned S3 and ArcticDB read as_of the recorded
  moment, then checked against the digest. It writes
  lineage/D31/{D}.json to the parity store.
- shadow.parity grants recompute_lineage only when both sides reproduce
  byte for byte, the record is bound to the sha256 of the graded objects,
  and every differing input itself grades v1_cause under its own key.
  An ArcticDB, set or one-sided differing input refuses. No band or
  tolerance is added.
- The step runs at the tail of shadow-sameday, after parity.

Refs nousergon/alpha-engine-config#11203

* feat(features): pin D31's numeric environment so its bytes are CPU-independent (alpha-engine-config-I11203)

Brian ruled on 2026-09-25 that no tolerance may absorb the recompute's
technical-group difference, and chose to pin the CPU math dispatch. He
accepted a one-time shift of about 1e-13 in v1's technical values.

Measured by replaying v1's own 2026-09-23 D31. Both that day's v1 and
shadow boxes were c5.large spot, per CloudTrail RunInstances.
- numpy 1.26.4 with AVX-512 on reproduces v1's published technical.parquet
  byte for byte. With AVX-512 masked, as on an AVX2-only AMD host, 3,433 cells
  differ, by up to 6.4e-13 relative.
- The four affected columns go through np.log (SIMD-dispatched) and pandas
  rolling loops. They make no BLAS call.
- The earlier 3,446-cell mismatch came from the replay host's numpy 2.4.6,
  not the box's numpy 1.26.4.
- Under the pin the technical group has a single SHA-256 across
  numpy 1.26.4 and 2.4.6, AVX-512 on or masked, BLAS at 1 or 4 threads, and
  SkylakeX or Haswell kernels.

What changed:
- features/numeric_pin.py is the one definition. It sets
  NPY_ENABLE_CPU_FEATURES to the build's baseline names, OPENBLAS_CORETYPE to
  Haswell, and the OpenBLAS, OMP and MKL thread counts to 1. It also clears
  NPY_DISABLE_CPU_FEATURES, because numpy refuses to import with both set.
  effective() measures what is actually in effect.
- weekly_collector.py, `python -m shadow` and `python -m features.compute`
  call apply() before numpy loads, but only when run as __main__.
- D31's frozen input record carries a numeric-env:// InputRef. It records the
  CPU model, instance type, numpy dispatch in effect, BLAS core and threads,
  libc, libm path and the pin.
- The recompute refuses by name when a run is unpinned, recorded no
  environment, or differs in numpy, BLAS, libc or libm.
- The data-spot box sources infrastructure/data_box_env.sh. It sets
  NE_DATA_INSTANCE_TYPE and NE_DATA_LIFECYCLE from IMDSv2, so manifests stop
  reading instance_type "local". It also exports the pin, derived from the
  module.

Keep the stage-coverage window across a spot relaunch (#1972)

The spot-interruption relaunch re-execs the launcher with `exec bash "$0"`.
_STAGE_WINDOW_START was not exported, so the relaunch recomputed it as "now"
and graded the execution's own auto-skipped output as STALE. On
rehearsal-2026-09-25-1 DataPhase1 that was six artifacts written by attempt 1
at 21:52-22:12Z, judged against attempt 2's 22:19:59Z window.

Export it in _spot_common.sh and in the spot_data_weekly.sh monolith, so a
relaunch keeps the execution's start and a fresh run still captures its own.
